issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no hardcoded coordinates. The new phase starts from random symmetric seeds and solves them with SLSQP using the existing cons/cjac. It then expands each solution to all 26 circles and polishes it with the full, unconstrained SLSQP before finalize(), so the validity checks are not bypassed.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The matrix M ties each circle a to circle h+a, reflected across the diagonal (x and y swapped), and gives both the same radius. This assumes v is laid out as [x(n), y(n), r(n)]. If it is laid out another way, the seeds are just a different feasible start and the full polish still fixes it. The symmetric phase cannot place a circle on the diagonal, which limits it but is not a correctness bug.
Side effect: the earlier penalty-continuation loop now gets only 30 s (60–90 s) instead of the full window. This is the likely cause of the drop in quality.

Candidate loss -2.6343 is worse than incumbent -2.6360 by 0.0017. One run each, so the spread is assumed from the stated ~1e-6 run-to-run noise. With that spread, z ≈ -0.0017/sqrt(2e-12) ≈ -1.2e3, consistent with the harness's -1195.5 (the small gap comes from rounding the means to 4 decimals). Rejecting is correct.
The incumbent's 2.6360 is a little above the stated best known 2.635. This is consistent with the literature value of about 2.6359 rounded, so it is not an integrity flag.
